trial_court: City Civil Judge, Bangalore, M.C. No. 259 of 1981
facts_of_case: The parties were married in Hyderabad. The husband filed for nullity of the marriage. The wife is seeking to transfer her case to be tried with her husband's case.

legal_principles.principle: The High Court has jurisdiction to transfer a suit pending in a Court subordinate to it to a Court subordinate to another High Court.
legal_principles.held: A Bench consisting of Stone C.J. and Vivian Bose, J., on reference by a Single Judge, have held that 'The High Court has jurisdiction to transfer a suit pending in a Court subordinate to it to a Court subordinate to another High Court.'
cited_cases: Firm Kanhaiyalal Daga -v.- Zumerlal and others, AIR 1940 Nagpur 145
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — applies to all courts with jurisdiction

legal_principles.principle: A High Court can order transfer of a case to some other Court under the different High Court.
legal_principles.held: Moreover, under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, it is held that 'The plain reading of this Section shows that in a situation like the present. High Court can order transfer of the case to some other Court under the different High Court.'
cited_cases: State Bank of India-v.- Sakow Industries Faridabad (Pvt) Ltd., AIR 1976 P and H 320 New Delhi
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — applies to courts with jurisdiction

outcome.final_order: The petition was allowed, and the case was transferred to the Court of the Chief Judge, City Civil Court at Hyderabad.

use_for_drafting: drafting a transfer petition in a matrimonial dispute
advising on joint trial of multiple petitions
assisting with a wife's petition for divorce
